provenance_summary: V1-B biological expansion wave. Microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) for heavy metal immobilization. Bacteria catalyze urea hydrolysis to produce carbonate ions that precipitate heavy metals.

mechanisms.name: MICP heavy metal immobilization
mechanisms.description: Bacteria catalyze urea hydrolysis producing CO₃²⁻ and NH₄⁺, which precipitate heavy metals as insoluble carbonates

pollutant_feature.text: Heavy metal ions (Pb²⁺, Cd²⁺, Cu²⁺, Zn²⁺)

bio_structure.text: Bacterial urease enzyme and cell surface

interaction.text: Urea hydrolysis produces CO₃²⁻ that precipitates heavy metals as carbonates

why_it_works.text: Microbial urease catalysis is highly efficient and can be controlled

causal_chain.transferable_principle: Microbial urease catalysis produces carbonate ions for heavy metal precipitation and immobilization

engineering_constraints.description: Bacterial culture: Sporosarcina pasteurii in urea-rich medium at 30°C

narrative.text: Microbially induced carbonate precipitation (MICP) uses bacterial urease to catalyze urea hydrolysis, producing carbonate ions that precipitate heavy metals as insoluble carbonates. This biomineralization process is used for soil remediation and wastewater treatment.

design_translation.idea: Use bacteria (Sporosarcina pasteurii) to catalyze urea hydrolysis for heavy metal precipitation and immobilization
examples: MICP for Pb²⁺ removal from wastewater
design_translation.applicability: Heavy metal removal from wastewater and soil remediation
